title: Reasons for the 2025 dengue decline and expansion of Project Wolbachia
asked: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked for the major reasons for the sharp decline in dengue cases in 2025 and when the Project Wolbachia trial will be extended to all towns in Singapore.
response: Ms Goh Hanyan said 4,036 dengue cases were reported in 2025, the lowest since 2018, due to an absence of major local outbreaks, a global decline in dengue cases, and collective efforts to control the mosquito population. Project Wolbachia will cover 740,000 households by March 2026, up from 580,000 in April 2025, and 800,000 households or 50% of all households by end-2026. In reply to supplementary questions, she said Wolbachia has reduced dengue transmission risk by more than 70% in release areas but is not a silver bullet, and that site selection and the pace of expansion depend on historical dengue data, local mosquito populations and finite resources.

key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: 4,036 dengue cases were reported in 2025, which was the lowest number since 2018.

key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: An absence of major local outbreaks locally, the global decline in dengue cases in 2025 and concerted efforts by all stakeholders and residents in Singapore to control the mosquito population, collectively contributed to the decrease.

key_points.point: Project Wolbachia will be expanded to cover 740,000 households by March 2026, up from 580,000 in April 2025.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: By March 2026, Project Wolbachia will be expanded to cover 740,000 households, up from 580,000 households in April 2025.

key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: By end-2026, Project Wolbachia will be released to cover 800,000 households or 50% of all households in Singapore, covering the majority of areas at risk of large dengue outbreaks.

key_points.point: Project Wolbachia has reduced dengue transmission risk by more than 70% in release areas.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: reducing the risks of dengue transmission by more than 70% in release areas.

key_points.point: Site selection for Wolbachia release is based on historical dengue situations and the current Aedes Aegypti mosquito population.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: site selection on areas to receive the Wolbachia Aedes mosquito release is based on multiple considerations, including historical dengue situations and the current Aedes Aegypti mosquito population.

key_points.point: Resources are finite and the pace of expansion is influenced by how quickly mosquito populations can be suppressed.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: Resources are finite and so the pace of expansion is also influenced by how quickly mosquito populations can be suppressed

key_points.point: Global dengue cases decreased from 14.4 million to five million.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: Globally, in 2025, we also saw a decrease in dengue cases from 14.4 million for the year before, to five million

key_points.point: NEA will announce new release sites in due course.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: NEA will announce the new sites in due course

key_points.point: Residents may see more mosquitoes during release periods, but these do not bite or transmit disease.
key_points.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
key_points.quote: more mosquitoes may be seen during the release periods of male Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, but these mosquitoes are necessary to help suppress the Aedes Aegypti population and do not bite or transmit disease.
